package_info.package_manager: Standalone Windows executable (not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malicious application distributed as a binary)
package_info.why_malicious: The application masquerades as a legitimate Coronavirus heat map viewer but covertly installs and runs the AZORult info stealer in the background, exfiltrating sensitive user data without consent.

execution_context.file_location: Main application binary (Coronavirus heat map app executable)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Process.Start('AZORult.exe'); // while displaying the legitimate map UI
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code launches the AZORult info stealer executable as a background process while displaying the legitimate Coronavirus map UI, enabling covert data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Launching a known info stealer in the background while presenting a legitimate interface is a classic malware tactic for evasion and data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate map application should not execute unrelated binaries, especially info stealers, or access sensitive user data without explicit consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers may launch helper processes, but not info stealers or unrelated executables.
key_indicators: Simultaneous display of legitimate UI and malicious activity
No user notification or consent for background process

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Collect browser credentials, cookies, and cryptocurrency wallet files; send via HTTP POST to C2 server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates and collects browser-stored credentials, cookies, and cryptocurrency wallet files, then exfiltrates this data to a remote command-and-control server via HTTP POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting sensitive credentials and exfiltrating them to an external server is a hallmark of info stealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications should not access or transmit browser credentials, cookies, or wallet files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise backup tools may access browser data with user consent, but never exfiltrate it to unknown servers.
key_indicators: Network communication to known C2 infrastructure
No user interaction or consent for data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: User downloads and launches the Coronavirus heat map application.
The application displays a legitimate map UI while silently launching the AZORult info stealer in the background.
AZORult collects sensitive data (credentials, cookies, wallet files) from the victim's machine.
AZORult exfiltrates the stolen data to a remote C2 server via HTTP POST.

behavioral_signatures: Legitimate-looking application launching known info stealer binaries
Simultaneous display of benign UI and background malicious process
Unauthorized access to browser credential stores and wallet files
Outbound HTTP POST requests to known AZORult C2 domains
file_indicators: Presence of AZORult.exe or similar payload in temp or user directories
Unexpected dropped executables alongside legitimate application files
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests to domains/IPs associated with AZORult C2 infrastructure
Unusual outbound traffic immediately after application launch
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for applications that launch secondary processes matching known info stealer signatures (e.g., AZORult.exe) while presenting benign UIs. Detect unauthorized access to browser credential stores and wallet files. Flag outbound HTTP POST requests to known C2 domains, especially following the execution of COVID-19 themed applications. Use endpoint protection to block known AZORult hashes and behavioral EDR rules to detect process injection or suspicious child process creation.
